# Runtime engines

What runs and hosts an agent, one spec each under `agentspecs/runtime-engines/`. An agent
spec names one with `runtime_engine:`, on the line after `harness:`; a spec that names
none, or another, is refused at load, and so is an engine asked to run a harness it does
not run. The [harness](../harnesses) says which agent program turns the agent's loop; the
runtime engine says what runs that program and keeps it alive. An engine that is not
enabled stays listed here and is not one an agent may name. The first enabled one is
the default: an agent built in code that names no engine runs there.

| Engine | Id | Harnesses | Enabled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Datalayer](https://datalayer.ai/docs/agents) | `datalayer` | any | yes |
| [Kagent](https://kagent.dev) | `kagent` | `pydantic-ai` | yes |
| [AWS AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/) | `agentcore` | `pydantic-ai` | yes |

## Each engine

### Datalayer (`datalayer`)

A Datalayer agent runtime, launched from the platform's pools or on your own machine, metered in credits and known by its uid.

### Kagent (`kagent`)

Kagent, a Kubernetes control plane for agents. The agent is a Kagent Agent (an AgentTemplate and a Harness running `agent-runtimes serve --target kagent` behind the Kagent bridge), reached through Kagent's A2A gateway at /agents/\{namespace\}/\{name\}; each conversation is a session actor of Agent Substrate, suspended when idle and resumed on the next message.

### AWS AgentCore (`agentcore`)

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime in the AWS account of the organization that launches the agent, the agent-runtimes image serving the spec (`agent-runtimes serve --target agentcore`); AgentCore starts it on each invocation, billed to that account.
